description: Evaluates whether an item constitutes excisable goods by testing its movability and its capability of being brought to the market to be bought and sold.
application_scenario: Use when determining if an intermediate product, captively consumed product, or permanently affixed structure attracts excise duty as manufactured goods. Do not use for determining the classification of an already recognized good.
reasoning_flow: Identify the specific product emerging from the manufacturing process.
Determine if the product is physically movable or permanently embedded to the earth.
Assess whether the product, in the exact form it emerges, is recognizable and capable of being bought and sold in the commercial market, placing the burden of proof on the revenue authority.
Conclude that the item is excisable goods only if it satisfies both the movability and marketability tests, regardless of whether it is actually sold or captively consumed.
example_application: A manufacturer produces a specialized chemical slurry that exists for 10 seconds before being pumped into a subsequent reaction chamber. The revenue department demands excise duty. Applying the test, the slurry is movable, but because it is highly unstable, cannot be stored, and has no recognized commercial market for purchase or sale, it fails the marketability test and is not an excisable good.
shared_pattern: In all three cases, the Court held that even if a product undergoes a manufacturing process, it does not become subject to excise duty unless it is both movable and capable of being marketed and sold in commercial parlance.
scope_exclusions: Not applicable to assessing the valuation of goods or determining the applicable tariff heading for undisputed goods.

description: Determines the classification of a product for taxation by applying the common, popular, or commercial understanding of the product rather than its strict scientific or technical definition.
application_scenario: Use when a statutory tariff entry uses everyday terminology without providing a specific technical definition, and there is a dispute between the scientific classification and how the trade and consumers view the product.
reasoning_flow: Identify the disputed tariff entries and the product being classified.
Check if the statute provides a specialized definition for the term. If not, proceed to the commercial parlance test.
Examine evidence of how the product is known, bought, sold, and used in the trade, market, and by the end consumer.
Reject classifications based solely on scientific composition or technical definitions if they contradict the popular understanding.
Classify the product based on its primary identity and function in commercial parlance.
example_application: A company manufactures a tomato based puree with added vitamins and claims it as a health supplement based on its chemical composition. The revenue department classifies it as ketchup. Applying the test, since consumers buy and use the product as a condiment for food, it is classified as ketchup under commercial parlance, overriding the technical chemical composition.
shared_pattern: In these cases, the Court rejected technical, scientific, or literal interpretations of product components, favoring how the product is identified and utilized by people conversant with the trade and everyday consumers.
scope_exclusions: Do not use if the governing statute expressly defines the term scientifically, or if the dispute relates to valuation rather than classification.

description: Evaluates a taxpayer's eligibility for a tax exemption by strictly construing the conditions of the exemption notification against the taxpayer at the threshold stage.
application_scenario: Use when a taxpayer claims a benefit, concession, or exemption under a specific statutory notification, and there is ambiguity regarding whether they meet the qualifying conditions.
reasoning_flow: Identify the specific exemption notification and the explicit conditions required to qualify for it.
Place the absolute burden of proof on the party claiming the exemption to demonstrate they fall entirely within its parameters.
Construe any ambiguity in the exemption's threshold applicability criteria strictly in favor of the revenue state and against the taxpayer.
Deny the exemption if the claimant fails to strictly satisfy all conditions.
example_application: A notification exempts software companies from service tax provided they submit an annual audit by March 31. A company submits it on April 2, arguing substantial compliance. Applying the strict construction doctrine at the threshold, the company failed to meet the explicit condition, so the exemption is denied.
shared_pattern: In all supporting cases, the Court strictly interpreted the qualifying conditions of exemption notifications, holding that the burden of proving strict compliance lies solely with the assessee.
scope_exclusions: Once the taxpayer has successfully proven they fall within the exemption clause, do not use strict construction to determine the scope of the benefit, which may receive a purposive or liberal construction.

description: Determines whether a process constitutes manufacture by analyzing if the raw materials undergo a substantial transformation resulting in a new commercial commodity.
application_scenario: Use when deciding if a secondary process applied to existing duty-paid materials amounts to the manufacture of a new product liable to fresh taxation.
reasoning_flow: Identify the original raw material and the specific physical or chemical process applied to it.
Assess the resulting product to determine if it has a distinct name, character, or use compared to the original material.
Evaluate whether the process is merely incidental or if it fundamentally transforms the article into a different commercial entity recognized by the market.
Conclude that manufacture has occurred only if a new and distinct commodity emerges. Otherwise, treat the process as non-manufacturing value addition.
example_application: A business buys large duty paid rolls of paper and cuts them into smaller sized sheets. Applying the transformation test, cutting paper does not yield a product with a new name, character, or use. It remains paper. Therefore, the cutting process does not amount to manufacture.
shared_pattern: These cases evaluate whether specific operations transform raw materials into new, distinct commercial commodities possessing a different character or use.
scope_exclusions: Not applicable to determining the assessable value of goods or applying general tariff classifications where the fact of manufacture is already admitted.

description: Applies the literal rule of interpretation to statutory notifications by refusing to import or imply restrictive words that the legislature chose to omit.
application_scenario: Use when a party attempts to narrow the scope of a plain statutory provision or exemption by reading in restrictive words like only, entirely, all, or generated within.
reasoning_flow: Analyze the exact text of the statutory provision or notification.
Identify the restrictive condition or qualifier that a party is attempting to read into the text.
Determine if the plain language of the statute naturally contains such a restriction.
If the language is plain and clear, enforce the text literally, refusing to rewrite the statute by implying words of limitation that the drafting authority did not explicitly include.
example_application: A tax exemption applies to vehicles using electric batteries. The tax authority denies the exemption to hybrid vehicles, arguing the exemption implies exclusively using electric batteries. Applying this reasoning flow, the court refuses to read the word exclusively into the statute, granting the exemption to the hybrid vehicle.
shared_pattern: In these cases, the Court refused the Revenue attempts to read unwritten restrictions into exemption notifications, such as reading only or exclusively into pig iron use, all into parts, and generated within into used within.
scope_exclusions: Do not use if the statutory provision is patently ambiguous, leads to a manifest absurdity, or if a purposive interpretation is mandated by the explicit objectives of the statute.
